security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, and documentation tables; no shell backtick execution is present. The real security concern is expected data transfer through the inference.sh CLI when prompts or images are sent to Gemini services.

remediation.suggestion: Document that prompts and images may be transmitted to inference.sh, Google Gemini, and Google Search when grounding is enabled. Warn users before submitting confidential media.
Keep guidance limited to the documented Gemini image app commands. Avoid encouraging arbitrary infsh operations or unreviewed flags.
Prefer saved input files or clear escaping guidance so copied prompts cannot break shell quoting.

static_findings.snippet: > Requires inference.sh CLI (`infsh`). Get installation instructions: `npx skills add inference-sh/s

semantic_findings.description: The skill allowlists Bash(infsh *) and instructs users to run Gemini image generation through inference.sh. Prompts and input images may leave the local environment for external processing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed tool pattern and examples clearly route prompts and images through a networked CLI. This is expected functionality, but it creates a real data-transfer risk for sensitive media.

content.user_title: Generate Gemini Images with Nano Banana 2
content.value_statement: Image generation workflows need clear model settings and repeatable prompts. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use Gemini image generation through inference.sh.
actual_capabilities: Runs Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview through the infsh CLI.
Creates images from text prompts with configurable image counts.
Edits supplied JPEG, PNG, or WebP images from image references.
Supports aspect ratio and resolution settings, including 1K, 2K, and 4K.
Can enable Google Search grounding for current visual context.
Shows Python SDK and streaming workflow examples for inference.sh.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account before use.
Sends prompts and input images to external services for processing.
Does not verify image rights, brand permissions, or legal clearance.
Output quality and availability depend on external model and service status.

use_cases.title: Concept Art Creation
use_cases.description: Create early visual directions from text prompts with chosen aspect ratios and resolutions.

use_cases.title: Product Image Iteration
use_cases.description: Edit supplied product images or generate multiple alternatives for review.

use_cases.title: Image Workflow Prototyping
use_cases.description: Test CLI and SDK image generation flows before integrating them into larger tools.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-2 to create one square image of [subject] in [style]. Include lighting, composition, colors, and mood.

prompt_templates.title: Create Design Variations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-2 to generate four image options for [project]. Use [aspect ratio] and keep the visual style consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-2 to edit this image: [image reference]. Change [specific element] while preserving [elements to keep].

prompt_templates.title: Build a Grounded Visual Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-2 with Google Search grounding to create a current visual concept for [timely topic]. Include settings and privacy cautions.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a wide concept image of a futuristic city at sunset.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a Gemini image generation request with a detailed scene prompt, a landscape aspect ratio, and external processing notice.

output_examples.input: A designer provides a product photo and asks to add a cleaner studio background.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares an image edit request that preserves the product while changing the background and lighting direction.

output_examples.input: A team asks for a weather-based poster concept using current information.
output_examples.output: The skill prepares a grounded visual request, enables current-context support, and reminds the user that results depend on external services.

best_practices: Use specific prompts with subject, style, lighting, composition, and output size.
Confirm that source images are authorized before sending them to external services.
Use saved input files for complex prompts to reduce shell quoting mistakes.
anti_patterns: Submitting confidential images without approval for external processing.
Copying commands with unescaped user text into a shell.
Expecting generated images to provide legal, brand, or copyright clearance.

faq.question: Does this skill require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill depends on the infsh CLI and an authenticated inference.sh account.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports image editing with supplied JPEG, PNG, or WebP image references.

faq.question: Can it generate multiple images?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show configurable image counts for variation generation.

faq.question: Does it support high resolution output?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented options include 1K, 2K, and 4K resolution settings.

faq.question: Does it send data outside my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and images may be sent to inference.sh and model providers for processing.

faq.question: Is Google Search grounding optional?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents a separate option for enabling current information grounding.
